newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees growth, balanced economy - fin. min..
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees growth, balanced economy - fin. min..

text.p: Hungarian Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said on Tuesday that the country's economy showed signs of increasing growth, while the balance of payments and the government budget preserved stability.
Medgyessy told the parliament that industrial output rose by more than six percent year-on-year in real terms in the first quarter of the year, while exports and imports rose by some eight percent.

"This indicates that there are no signs of an excessive increase in imports," he said, adding that machinery and energy imports rose dynamically. "This is in a natural correlation with increasing economic growth."

Medgyessy said the gross domestic product (GDP) increased by three percent in the last quarter of 1996 and this year's figures showed that GDP growth is likely to reach 2.5 percent this year, compared with some one percent in 1996.
He said the deficit of the social security reached 25.8 billion forints in the first four months of this year, compared with a forecast of 16.5 billion forints for that period.
But the central state budget deficit was 145 billion forints, against a 174 billion forecast, he added.
He said inflation, which ran at 18.6 percent in April, was going down according to the government's projections, while wages grew slightly more rapidly than planned.
"But we do not see a danger in that as corporate performance and GDP growth is also better than we calculated."
